syllabus.clause: immutable micro-partitions (50–500 MB uncompressed) with per-column metadata, pruning, clustering depth and automatic clustering, search optimization; time travel, fail-safe and zero-copy cloning as consequences of immutable storage; secure data sharing without copies.

at.step: Reveal: clustering depth and automatic clustering
Reveal: zero-copy cloning and secure data sharing

items.item: All data in Snowflake tables is automatically divided into micro-partitions, contiguous units of storage, fifty to five hundred megabytes of uncompressed data each
The micro-partition metadata maintained by Snowflake enables precise pruning of columns at query run-time, including semi-structured data
Clustering depth measures the average depth of overlapping micro-partitions; an empty table has a clustering depth of zero

at.step: Reveal: clustering depth and automatic clustering

items.item: Automatic Clustering is the Snowflake service that continually manages reclustering of clustered tables, suspendable per table, needing no user-provided warehouse

at.step: Reveal: clustering depth and automatic clustering

sources.source: Snowflake docs, Speeding up queries of structured data with search optimization

items.item: The search optimization service improves point-lookup and substring queries, a mechanism distinct from clustering and pruning

sources.source: Snowflake docs, Understanding & using Time Travel

items.item: Time Travel accesses historical data within a defined retention period; one day by default, up to ninety days for permanent objects on paid editions

sources.source: Snowflake docs, Understanding and viewing Fail-safe

items.item: Fail-safe is a non-configurable seven-day last-resort recovery window after Time Travel ends, reachable only through Snowflake Support
Clones share the same underlying storage as the source table

at.step: Reveal: zero-copy cloning and secure data sharing

sources.source: Snowflake docs, About Secure Data Sharing

items.item: No actual data is copied or transferred between accounts; all shared objects stay read-only to the consumer
